1 ثَبِطَ , aor.
ثَبَطَ , [inf. n., accord. to rule, ثَبْطٌ,] (K,) or, as Sgh says, [judging from the part. n. ثَبِطٌ,] thus analogy requires that it should be, (TA,) He was, or became, stupid in his work, or action; and weak: and he (a man, and a horse, K and TA, said of a horse with respect to covering,
TA) was, or became, heavy, sluggish, or slow. (K, * TA.) ＝
-A2- See also 2, in two places.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
